title: Symplectic Weil Representation over a Finite Field
body_html:
Symplectic Weil Representation over a Finite Field

Let $(E,j)$ be a nondegenerate symplectic space of dimension $2\ell$ over a finite field $k$ of odd order $q$. Let $H(E,j)$ be its Heisenberg group, let $S(E,j)$ be its symplectic group acting as automorphisms of $H(E,j)$, and let $SH(E,j) = S(E,j) \ltimes H(E,j)$ be their semidirect product. Let $Z$ be the center of $H(E,j)$, write its elements as $e_x$ for $x \in k$, let $\xi$ be a nontrivial character of $Z$, and let $\eta_\xi^{E,j}$ be the class of irreducible representations of $H(E,j)$ with central character $\xi$ (the Stone--von Neumann class).

Theorem (Gérardin).

(a) Existence and uniqueness. There is a unique class $W_\xi^{E,j}$ of representations of $S(E,j)$, called the Weil representation of $S(E,j)$ associated to $\xi$, characterized by:

  • (a′) for every realization $\tau$ of $\eta_\xi^{E,j}$, there is a representation of $SH(E,j)$ on the space of $\tau$ that restricts to $\tau$ on $H(E,j)$ and whose restriction to $S(E,j)$ belongs to $W_\xi^{E,j}$;

together with, in the single exceptional case $\ell = 1$, $q = 3$, the normalization

  • (a″) $W_\xi^{E,j}$ is disjoint from its complex conjugate.

For $(\ell,q) \neq (1,3)$ the extension in (a′) is automatically unique, by irreducibility of $\eta_\xi^{E,j}$ together with the fact that $S(E,j)$ then equals its own commutator subgroup; so (a′) alone determines $W_\xi^{E,j}$, and (a″) is needed only to remove the residual ambiguity when $\ell = 1$, $q = 3$.

(b) Parabolic construction. Let $E_+ \subseteq E$ be a nontrivial totally isotropic subspace, with stabilizer $P(E_+,j) \subseteq S(E,j)$ (a parabolic subgroup, maximal when $E_+$ is Lagrangian), and let $\chi_{E_+}$ be the character $s \mapsto (\det_{E_+} s)^{(q-1)/2}$ of $P(E_+,j)$. Let $\pi_+$ be the representation of $P(E_+,j)\,H(E,j)$ obtained by inducing the $\chi_{E_+}$-twisted pull-back of a representation, chosen as in (a′), of the semidirect product over the reduced symplectic space $E_+^{\perp}/E_+$ attached to $E_+$. Then there is a unique representation of $SH(E,j)$ on the space of $\pi_+$ that agrees with $\pi_+$ on $P(E_+,j)\,H(E,j)$, and its restriction to $S(E,j)$ belongs to $W_\xi^{E,j}$.

(c) Restriction to a Siegel--Levi subgroup. Let $E = E_+ \oplus E_-$ be a Witt decomposition, and let $G$ be the stabilizer of both $E_+$ and $E_-$ in $S(E,j)$; then $G \cong GL(E_+)$ (with $E_-$ identified with the dual of $E_+$ via $j$), and

$$ W_\xi^{E,j}\big|_{G} \;\cong\; \chi_G \otimes W_G, $$

where $\chi_G$ is the unique nontrivial one-dimensional real character of $G$ and $W_G$ is the general-linear Weil representation of $G$.

(d) Dependence on the central character. For nontrivial characters $\xi'$ and $\xi''$ of $Z$, one has $W_{\xi'}^{E,j} \cong W_{\xi''}^{E,j}$ if and only if $\xi'$ and $\xi''$ are conjugate by a nonzero square of $k$, that is, $\xi''(e_x) = \xi'(e_{t^2 x})$ for some $t \in k^*$ and all $x \in k$. Consequently there are exactly two classes $W_\xi^{E,j}$, indexed by the two square classes of $k^*$.

The linearization argument (the $p$-Sylow extension criterion) and the explicit Fourier--Gaussian normalization underlying (a) and (b) are recorded in Gérardin Linearization of the Finite Symplectic Weil Cocycle.
